Send an email to Accessibility (accommodation requests only; other inquiries won't receive a response). Regular or Temporary: Regular Language Fluency: English (Required) Work Shift: 1st shift (United States of America) Please review the following job description: Senior leader responsible for end-to-end production operations, stability, and resiliency across Truist’s Enterprise Payments application portfolio — a mission-critical ecosystem enabling real-time movement of client funds across ACH, wire, and instant payment rails. This portfolio represents one of the most operationally critical segments within Truist, with a high concentration of Tier 1 systems, money-movement platforms, and SOX-regulated applications, directly impacting client liquidity, financial risk, and firm reputation. Leads a large production support organization of full-time and contingent resources and serves as the single accountable production support leader for Enterprise Payments, partnering closely with application delivery to ensure 24x7x365 availability, rapid incident response, and end-to-end operational integrity, while continuously improving resiliency across payment systems. This role is both operational and transformational. The leader is accountable for maintaining stability across highly available systems while driving the evolution of the production support operating model through automation - advancing toward a modern, automation-first, engineering-aligned model aligned to modern DevSecOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) principles, with accountability for improving resiliency and non-functional requirements across the application lifecycle. This includes establishing SLO/SLI frameworks and reliability governance, and driving continuous improvement of non-functional requirements such as availability, recoverability, and performance, while expanding observability, AI-driven operations, and intelligent automation across production support functions to reduce manual toil and enable self-healing capabilities. Serves as the senior escalation point for major incidents and operational risk, providing clear executive-level communication on system health and influencing enterprise priorities through a lens of stability, resilience, and business impact. Essential Duties And Responsibilities Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time. Manages a single technology operations job area, overseeing multiple teams led by mid to upperlevel managers to deliver secure, reliable services that support business objectives. Establishes short to midterm operational plans for the technology operations job area and recommends strategies and priorities that align with enterprise and corporate technology direction. Manages the execution of technology strategies defined by executives and senior management within the job area, translating them into clear goals, roadmaps, and delivery expectations for managed teams. Implements and refines governance, risk management, and compliance practices for the job area, ensuring alignment with enterprise frameworks and effective control execution. Oversees key technology initiatives and operational improvement programs within the job area, delivering measurable gains in stability, efficiency, and business value. Partners with senior leaders and stakeholders to share operational insights, performance trends, and risk perspectives from the job area, informing adjustments to broader technology and business plans. Leads innovation within the job area by defining and promoting improved standards, processes, and operating models, and by driving adoption of automation and relevant emerging technologies. Owns key vendor, partner, and stakeholder relationships for the job area, influencing contract outcomes, service levels, and investments to meet operational and financial objectives. Monitors operational performance and financial results for the job area, managing to an approved budget and leading continuous improvement to optimize cost, quality, resilience, and colleague experience. Provides leadership, coaching, and development for managers and senior individual contributors within the job area, building the capabilities needed to execute current and future plans. Bachelor’s degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or related field. Minimum of 12 years of progressive experience in technology operations. Track record of building and transforming large production support organizations from manual, tiered support models to automated, DevSecOps-aligned operating models. We offer fair and transparent pay, benchmarked to the market. Truly global. We work across continents and time zones, with teammates and customers from all over the world. You will run campaigns that cross borders, cultures, and languages, and see your ideas land worldwide. Growth built in. Clear goals, open feedback and personal development plans. We support your progress with learning opportunities and by covering role-specific events, from design conferences to marketing forums. Team offsites. Sometimes just Slack is not enough. That is why we meet in person a few times a year. Trips are fully covered, so you can meet, collaborate, and recharge together. Getting you set up. We make sure you have access to the tools and hardware you need to do your work well. Friendly by design. Our logo is a dog for a reason. We keep things human, open and kind. We welcome individuality, quirks and different perspectives, because that is what makes our work smarter and more fun. Your communication is second to none, and you're always thinking one step ahead when it comes to delivering an event, pre-event and on-site. You understand the importance of an event running smoothly, and love learning as you go to optimise for the future. This role is perfect for somebody looking for their next step up: a hands-on IC role where you’ll play a lead role in some of our largest flagship events across EMEA, and pitch in on general team tasks day to day. You'll run established event formats independently and apply good judgement within known processes, while leaning on your manager for guidance on new or first-of-their-kind activations. If that sounds like your kind of thing, we want to hear from you! Coordinate invitation strategy, registration, attendee communications and internal promotion so the right people show up, market by market.
